note: When each street was last resurfaced. Hand-maintained: there is no public dataset of last-repaved dates for municipal streets, so every entry here is traced to a named grant award or a published construction notice. Keys are street names spelled as `crossing_street` spells them in the survey CSV. A street absent from `streets` has NO known paving date -- that is the normal case, not an error. Read `coverage` before using any of this to rank anything.
coverage: 7 of the 35 streets carrying a surveyed crossing have a date here. The other 28 -- including West Broad Street, where the worst conditions are -- are unknown. Fill them from the Borough Clerk's paving history (and, for a borough with one, the road-opening moratorium list, which is effectively a recent-paving list) and from the County Engineer for CR 518 west of Greenwood Avenue.
caveats: A grant AWARD year is not a construction year. NJDOT Municipal Aid money is typically built the following construction season or the one after, so treat `year` from `njdot_municipal_aid` as 'no earlier than'.

Dates are recorded per street, but paving happens per segment. East Broad Street's 2024 county resurfacing ran Elm Street to Greenwood Avenue only; the entry's `limits` field says so. Anything outside stated limits is not covered by that date.
Absence of a date says nothing about condition. It means nobody has looked it up.

cycles.note: Used to estimate how long until a street would next be resurfaced. Both figures are benchmarks, not published local policy -- see `verified` on each.
cycles.county_verified: NOT VERIFIED as published policy. Mercer County's Highway Division describes a condition-driven pavement management system across 180 centerline miles and publishes no cycle length or forward schedule. 10 years is the low end of the standard 10-20 year service life for a full mill-and-overlay, and is used here as a working assumption. Confirm with the County Engineer before quoting it.
cycles.borough_verified: NOT VERIFIED. Hopewell Borough publishes no pavement management program or paving schedule; its repaving is visibly grant-driven at roughly one street per year against 35+ streets, which is a far longer de facto cycle than 15 years. Neighbouring Hopewell Township prioritises roads by the probability the road stays in good shape for 10-15 years, which is the closest local benchmark found.
